title: Even Rama falls
hook: arrows from an empty sky, and Rama, God on earth, falls like a man
carry: the avatar lives a real human life

segments.voice: Yesterday: the siege. Lanka surrounded, and still Angada carried one last offer before the battle began. Sama first: peace before force.

The first day of fighting goes badly for Lanka. Duel after duel, the monkey and bear leaders win, and the rakshasa champions fall or run. The sun sets, and the fighting goes on in the dark, by the light of weapons. In one duel, Angada smashes the chariot of Ravana's son, killing his horses and driver. The prince jumps clear. Then he does something the monkeys have no answer for. He disappears.
screen: `A GOOD FIRST DAY.` → `FIGHTING IN THE DARK.` → `HE DISAPPEARS.`

segments.voice: His name is Indrajit, conqueror of Indra, king of the gods; the epic says he once carried Indra off as a captive. Now he rises out of sight among the clouds and starts shooting. Valmiki says the arrows turn into serpents as they strike, wrapping Rama and Lakshmana tight, until the two brothers can't move. They fall side by side, covered in shafts. Sugriva, Hanuman and Jambavan gather around them, stunned. Indrajit shouts down that they're dead, and goes home to tell his father. Stop on that picture, because it's strange. For Hindus, Rama is Vishnu himself, come down to earth. That's what avatar means: a descent. So how can God lie bound on a battlefield? The story's answer, as Hindus hear it, is that the descent is real. Rama doesn't pretend to be human; he lives it. At the very end of the war, when the gods come to praise him, Rama says: I think of myself as a man, Rama, son of Dasharatha. Many Hindu teachers read that as the heart of the avatar: God doesn't watch a human life from above, he goes all the way in, fear, grief and defeat included. And Valmiki doesn't rush to the rescue. The first night of the war ends with the heroes down, the sky quiet, and nobody sure whether they're alive. That's why a Hindu can pray to Rama on the worst night of a hard year. He has lain on that field. A fall doesn't mean God has gone; in this story, God is the one lying there.
screen: `INDRAJIT: CONQUEROR OF INDRA.` · `THE BROTHERS FALL.` · `I THINK OF MYSELF AS A MAN.` · `GOD GOES ALL THE WAY IN.` · then, large: `THE AVATAR LIVES A REAL HUMAN LIFE.`

segments.voice: When a hard stretch comes, many Hindu families simply say Rama's name, over and over. Sit low and steady, and on each slow out-breath say Ram, softly, picturing the brothers on the field, not yet risen. If you don't pray, picture them anyway and breathe with them: down, and not alone.
Indrajit's arrows. Shot by Ravana's son from out of sight, they bind Rama and Lakshmana, and God on earth falls like a man.
Your line: the avatar lives a real human life. Next, Ravana tries to use the fall against Sita. Day six hundred forty-one, done.

fork.setup: your little cousin sees a picture of Rama bound by serpents and asks: if rama is God, how did he lose? what fits?
options: as Rama, God lives a real human life, falls and all.
it was a trick; he only pretended to be hurt.
Indrajit was simply stronger than God.
fork.reveal: avatar means descent. Valmiki's Rama says, i think of myself as a man. he truly falls, and truly rises.

original.note: Sanskrit avatāra: a descent, from ava, down, and tṛ, to cross: God coming down into the world.

trapdoor: what you thought: if Rama is God, the fall was just for show.
what it means: the avatar is a real descent; Rama lives a fully human life, defeat included.
what a scholar hears: in Yuddha Kanda 117 Rama tells the gods, ātmānaṃ mānuṣaṃ manye: i think of myself as a man.

Indrajit.meaning: Ravana's son; the name means conqueror of Indra

Meghanada.meaning: Indrajit's birth name: one who roars like a thundercloud

Indra.meaning: king of the gods in the old stories

Jambavan.meaning: the old bear king, a wise elder in Rama's army

avatar.meaning: a descent; God coming down to live in the world, as Vishnu does as Rama

recall: the forest ascetic who waited for Rama
jaw, the root of Hanuman's name
